auditor: independent read-only general agent (adversarial), adjudicated by the main agent

findings.problem: PIECE/LE3/EMPTY counts sum the bit VALUES (2 and 4) instead of counting rows, so masks.json and the I3 assertion are 2x/4x too large; every real run assert-fails.
findings.fix: count with ((flags & BIT) != 0).sum(); verified on real data: PIECE 0.1517, LE3 0.0230, EMPTY 0.0938 of 21 378 590 rows.

findings.problem: The plan's row->token formula (t0+4+r) is wrong: soft rows are per WORD, tokens are per PIECE. Measured: that formula yields 34.1 % piece targets, the word-aware grouping yields 15.3 % (= audit_signal.json), and 54.4 % of rows are placed at the wrong logits position by train.py.
findings.fix: word-aware grouping (join ## continuations); target = first token of the word, pos = first token index - 1; new --emit-align / distill_align= in train.py. Plan §2.3 and §3 rewritten; V9 added.

findings.problem: The chi-square STATISTIC was printed and stored as p_chi2, so consumers read 0.017 as a p-value when the p-value is 0.895.
findings.fix: report chi2_stat and p_chi2_cc = erfc(sqrt(stat/2)) (df=1); covered by test_chi2_with_cc_is_a_probability.

findings.problem: Values outside {0,1} exit 2, but typing_eval.rs writes -1 for metrics a mode does not compute, so typing dumps were unprocessable.
findings.fix: drop negative values per metric, report dropped/n, exit 2 only if <2 rows remain; tested.

findings.problem: rows=N sampled min(target_sentences, n) sentences once, so short sentences could fall below N.
findings.fix: draw in rounds over not-yet-picked indices until cumulative rows >= N; N > total exits non-zero; test_slice_data.py.

findings.problem: The CE gate assigned tgt[b,j] in a Python loop over ~10k elements per step (with a GPU sync per assignment), which would have destroyed throughput.
fill/unigram defaulted to a hard-coded de_unigram.npz that §2.2 never produces.
findings.fix: default is <soft_stem>.unigram.npz next to the soft file; --unigram overrides.

findings.evidence: Recomputed on 3000 sentences with the word-aware target: 0.8727 over ALL rows; over FILLED rows 0.8727/0.9061 = 0.9634 ~= 0.9643. The auditor included the 9.4 % empty rows. The plan now states the denominator explicitly.

Recomputed 491 321 / 21 378 590 = 0.02298 over all rows with (probs>0).sum() <= 3. audit_signal.json (0.0254) is a different cut/denominator and is treated as stale; the plan quotes the recomputed value and the definition.

findings.problem: Offset sentinel 0 is ambiguous with soft row 0.
Test and build asserted different PIECE windows.
findings.fix: single word-aware expectation [0.145,0.165]; real smoke recomputes target/pos independently.

findings.evidence: Pre-existing in HEAD, not a regression; changing it would break the bit-equality contract and is out of scope.

findings.problem: The R4 bit-equality test relies on git plumbing that misbehaves with Windows-style worktree paths.
findings.evidence: The test resolves the worktree .git pointer and reads HEAD blobs via cat-file; it passes. Documented in the results doc as WSL-only.

new_findings_from_verification.problem: train.py's Soft.batch() places soft row r at logits position 3+r, but rows are per word while positions are per token. Measured on 3000 sentences: 54.4 % of rows land on the wrong position, 72.1 % of sentences are affected, and every KD target after the first piece-spelled word is shifted.
new_findings_from_verification.fix: distill_align= (opt-in) scatters each row at its word-aware position; default path bit-identical (tested).

new_findings_from_verification.problem: No test covered finding 1 (flag counts vs bits), so the suite stayed green while masks.json was wrong.
new_findings_from_verification.fix: test_soft_mask.InvariantsBitwise.test_counts_match_flags compares masks.json counts with the npz flags row counts.

verdict: NO_OPEN_HIGH_CONFIDENCE_FINDINGS after fixes; all high findings fixed, 2 rejected with evidence, 2 accepted as documented limitations.
